To achieve a CTL of 60 safely, we will target a conservative ramp rate of +1 to +2 CTL points per week. coach_verdict: Given your suppressed HRV of 28 ms, we are prioritizing physiological safety and aerobic base building today (70/30 pyramidal rule). Priority 1 is a structured Zone 2 Cycling session to accumulate aerobic volume with minimal autonomic stress. Priority 2 is a dedicated Strength session to build torque and structural durability for your cycling and running goals. Priority 3 is a conditional VO2max Running session, only to be touched if your warmup feels exceptionally fluid and your resting HR stabilizes.

priority_1.workout_details: 10 min warm-up progressing to 140W. 60 min steady state at 175W (68% FTP) maintaining a cadence of 90-95 RPM. 5 min cool-down below 130W. Total duration: 75 minutes.
priority_1.reason: This is the safest and most effective way to accumulate CTL today. It respects your low HRV (28 ms) by keeping autonomic stress low while strengthening your aerobic engine, aligning directly with the 70% aerobic base requirement.

priority_2.workout_details: 3 rounds of: 5x Barbell Back Squats @ 80kg, 5x Romanian Deadlifts @ 75kg. Followed by 3 rounds of: 8x Heavy Sandbag Cleans (70kg), 10x Kettlebell Goblet Squats (20kg), 12x Hanging Knee Raises. 2 min rest between sets.
priority_2.reason: Excellent alternative to cardiovascular training today. Heavy strength work targets recruitment of high-threshold motor units to support cycling torque and running power without imposing high cardiorespiratory stress on your recovery systems.

priority_3.workout_details: 15 min easy jogging warm-up. 5x 3-minute intervals at 5km target pace (target HR >175 bpm) with 3-minute walking recoveries. 10 min easy jog cool-down.
priority_3.reason: A high-intensity quality session to target your 5km running goal. This is ranked third and is strictly conditional. Only perform this if you feel highly motivated, pain-free, and your HR responds normally during the warm-up.
